title: Cylindrical coordinates
section: Analytic Geometry of R3 ▷ Cylindrical Coordinates
terms: cylindrical coordinates; cylindrical radius; azimuthal angle; coordinate surface.

exposition.text:
Cylindrical coordinates (r,θ, z) combine polar coordinates in the xy-plane with height: x =
2 2 2
r cos θ, y = r sin θ, r ≥ 0, and z is unchanged. Thus r = x + y . The angle is defined modulo
2π, and is arbitrary on the z-axis.
The surface r = a > 0 is a circular cylinder, while z = c is a horizontal plane. With r ≥ 0, a
fixed value of θ gives a vertical half-plane bounded by the z-axis, not the whole plane. Cylin-
drical coordinates are especially efficient for rotational symmetry; angle-dependent expressions
2 2 2 2
may simplify through r cos 2θ = x − y and r sin 2θ = 2xy.

question.text:
2
The surface z = r sin(2θ) is intersected by y = x. What is the resulting relation between z and
x?
2 2 2 2
(A) z = x (B) z = 2x (C) z = −2x (D) z = 4x (E) z = 0

solution.text:
2 2
r sin 2θ = 2(r cos θ)(r sin θ) = 2xy. Substituting y = x gives z = 2x .
